subject: general
question: Which freedom fighter of British India is widely regarded as the "father of the two-nation theory"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Syed Ahmed Khan.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Syed Ahmed Khan:-**__

 __
 
• He was a Muslim scholar, social reformer, and educationalist in British India.
 
• He was one of the first Muslim intellectuals to argue that Hindus and Muslims were two distinct nations with different cultures and values.
 
• He believed that Muslims could not prosper in a united India dominated by Hindus, and that they needed a separate homeland where they could practice their religion and culture freely.
 
• **He is widely regarded as the "father of the two-nation theory". (Hence option 2 is correct)**
 
• Khan's two-nation theory was later adopted by the Muslim League, led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
 
• The Muslim League campaigned for the creation of a separate Muslim state in British India, which eventually led to the partition of India and the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:-**

 
 
• He was an Indian anti-colonial nationalist, secular humanist, social democrat, and author who was a central figure in India during the middle of the 20th century.
 
• **Nehru was a principal leader of the Indian nationalist movement in the 1930s and 1940s. Upon India's independence in 1947, he served as the country's first prime minister for 17 years. **
 
• Nehru promoted parliamentary democracy, secularism, and science and technology during the 1950s, powerfully influencing India's arc as a modern nation.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:-**
 
 
• **He was one of the pioneers of the Indian independence movement. He is considered the "Father of Indian Unrest" by the British.**
 
• Tilak was a staunch nationalist and believed that India should be independent from British rule.
 
• He was a leading figure in the Swadeshi movement, which promoted the use of Indian-made goods instead of British goods.
 
• He also founded the Home Rule League, which demanded self-government for India.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Ali Jinnah:-**
 
 
• **He was a Pakistani barrister, politician and statesman who is widely regarded as the founder of Pakistan.**
 
• Jinnah was initially a member of the Indian National Congress (INC), but he became disillusioned with the party's secular policies. He believed that Muslims needed their own political party to represent their interests.
